{{nihongo|'''Yamaguni Shrine'''|山国神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tanba Province]].

'''Yamaguni Shrine''' (やまぐにじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Keihoku Torii-chō, {{ill|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|ar|أوكيو-كو (كيوتو)|arz|اوكيو-كو, كيوتو|ca|Ukyō|ceb|Ukyō-ku|de|Ukyō-ku (Kyōto)|eo|Kvartalo Ukjo|eu|Ukyō-ku (Kyoto)|fa|اوکیو، کیوتو|fi|Ukyō-ku|fr|Ukyō-ku|fy|Ukyo-ku|id|Ukyō-ku, Kyōto|it|Ukyō-ku|ja|右京区|ko|우쿄구|my|အုခယောရပ်ကွက်၊ ကျိုတို|nl|Ukyo-ku|nn|Ukyo-ku i Kyoto|ru|Укё (Киото)|tr|Ukyō|uk|Район Укьо|ur|اوکیؤ وارڈ، کیوٹو|war|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|wuu|右京区|zh|右京區|zh_yue|右京區|qid=Q580186}}, {{ill|Kyoto|Q34600|qid=Q34600}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank}} it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.

Yamaguni forestry area|ja|山国荘|qid=Q21019706|lt=the Yamaguni forestry area}}, and it is said that during the {{ill|Hōki|de|Hōki (Ära)|es|Hōki (nengō)|fa|هوکی (دوره)|fr|Ère Hōki|ia|Hoki (era)|id|Hōki|ja|宝亀|ko|호키 (연호)|pt|Hōki (era)|ru|Хоки (нэнго)|simple|Hōki|sr|Хоки|tr|Hōki|uk|Хокі|zh|寶龜|zh_yue|寶龜|qid=Q18520676}} era (770–780) the {{ill|Bureau of Repairs|Q6668859|qid=Q6668859}} constructed the main hall. During its construction, {{ill|Wake no Kiyomaro|Q7961005|qid=Q7961005}} served as the chief officiant. In {{ill|1016|Q19247|qid=Q19247}} ({{ill|Chōwa|Q1194173|qid=Q1194173}} 5), {{ill|Emperor Sanjō|Q357231|qid=Q357231}} bestowed upon the shrine the divine rank of Senior First Rank, designated it as a place of imperial prayer, and granted the chrysanthemum crest. This crest can still be seen on items such as the mikoshi used in the autumn festival.  
The shrine was destroyed during the {{ill|Genpei War|Q737542|qid=Q737542|lt=Genpei War}}, but was rebuilt in {{ill|1233|Q5421|qid=Q5421}} ({{ill|Tenpuku|Q1194452|qid=Q1194452|lt=Tempuku}} 1) by {{ill|Emperor Shijō|Q374020|qid=Q374020}}. However, in {{ill|1333|Q6004|qid=Q6004}} ({{ill|Genkō (1331–1334)|Q1194556|qid=Q1194556}} 3 / {{ill|Shōkyō|Q1069086|qid=Q1069086}} 2), it was again destroyed during the {{ill|Genkō War|Q1432624|qid=Q1432624}}.  
In {{ill|1370|Q6217|qid=Q6217}} ({{ill|Ōan|Q1146245|qid=Q1146245}} 3), {{ill|Hosokawa Yoriyuki|Q1139739|qid=Q1139739}}, a retainer of {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Q248381|qid=Q248381}}, went into seclusion in {{ill|Yamaguni-shō|ja|山国荘|qid=Q21019706}}. Upon his reinstatement three years later, he petitioned for the restoration of the shrine, and in {{ill|1399|Q6422|qid=Q6422}} ({{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 6) the shrine buildings were repaired and an imperial edict ({{ill|rinji|Q11607250|qid=Q11607250}}) was granted. At this time, Ashikaga Yoshimitsu dedicated the “two horizontal bars within a circle” crest, which has since been used as the shrine’s emblem.  
The shrine was again destroyed during the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Warring States period}}, but was rebuilt in {{ill|1596|Q6785|qid=Q6785}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 1) by {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|Q349440|qid=Q349440}}.<br />
In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6) it was designated a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in {{ill|1900|Q2034|qid=Q2034}} (Meiji 33) it was promoted to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}} status. During this period, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fujino Itsuki}}, a Western Army liaison of the {{ill|Yamaguni Corps|Q11467675|qid=Q11467675}}, served as chief priest. Today, Itsuki’s great-great-grandson continues to serve as the shrine’s chief priest.
